# Isolate Vocals from a Song

- Route: `/tools/isolate-vocals-from-song`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `isolate-vocals-from-song`

## Summary

Extract vocals from music tracks for remixes, covers, transcription, and analysis. Use only on music you have the right to. (Audio tools)

## Details

AI-based source separation can pull a vocal track out of a finished mix — great for remixes, covers, karaoke prep, or transcribing lyrics. Media Manipulator runs the separation on our own GPU server. The result is a single vocal stem you can download and use anywhere — as long as you have the right to do so for your source material.
### What it does
- Runs AI-based source separation to extract the vocal track from a music recording.
- Outputs a single isolated vocal stem in the same format as your file (MP3 stays MP3), or in FLAC, WAV or MP3 if you choose.
- Pairs well with audio cleanup tools like denoise and EQ for a polished result.
- Supports WAV, MP3, FLAC, M4A, OGG, OPUS, and more inputs.
### How to use it
1. Upload song: Drop in any common audio file with mixed vocals + music.
2. Run AI separation: Local GPU model splits vocals from the rest of the mix.
3. Clean up (optional): Apply denoise, EQ, or gain to polish the stem.
4. Download vocal stem: Save the isolated vocals: same format as your file by default, or FLAC, WAV or MP3.
### Technical details
- Source separation is inherently imperfect — reverb, harmonies, and heavy effects bleed into the output.
- An MP3 or other compressed file comes back in its own format (MP3 at 320 kbps). Lossless files (WAV, FLAC, AIFF) come back as FLAC. FLAC and WAV keep the most detail for further editing in a DAW; WAV is the largest.
- For karaoke (instrumental only), use the dedicated "Remove Vocals" mode in the audio converter instead.
### Use cases
- Remixes and covers: Build a new instrumental around an isolated vocal.
- Lyric and melody transcription: Get a clearer signal for hand or AI transcription.
- Karaoke prep: Pair the isolated vocal with a separate instrumental version.
- Audio engineering practice: Study mixing technique on commercial recordings.
### FAQ
Q: Is this fully clean separation?
A: No source separation tool is perfect. Expect some artifacts, especially around heavy reverb and harmonies. Choose FLAC or WAV output if you plan to clean the stem up afterward in a DAW.
Q: What audio formats are supported?
A: WAV, MP3, FLAC, M4A/AAC, OGG, OPUS, and most other common audio formats.
Q: Can I use this on copyrighted music?
A: Only if you own the rights, have a license, or are operating under fair use in your jurisdiction. You are responsible for how you use the output.
Q: Where can I get just the instrumental?
A: Use the "Remove Vocals" AI mode in the audio converter — same upload, different output.
